text: In Genesis 22 a question is raised which the narrator never answers. Abraham is commanded to take his son, his only son, whom he loves; and of what he feels upon that command no account is given, the narrator never once entering into his mind, so that Abraham is presented less as a character than as a silence, and upon that silence the whole chapter turns. He makes no protest, and he attempts no bargain; there is nothing here of the man who argued on behalf of Sodom.
